summary: I sent the exact multi-step auth request to Claude Code in a fresh session. The agent loaded `hyperpowers:brainstorming` first and wrote a design spec. It then loaded `hyperpowers:writing-plans` and said "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan." No implementation code had been written by then. The plugin under test calls itself "hyperpowers", so I counted `hyperpowers:writing-plans` as the skill the criterion calls `superpowers:writing-plans`.
reasoning: The criterion needs a writing-plans skill load that comes before any implementation code. The session log shows Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans was called after the brainstorming skill, a design spec and a .gitignore were written, and no application code (app.js or new route files) had been written or changed. The namespace mismatch (hyperpowers vs superpowers) comes from how this plugin build is named, not from the agent's behaviour, so I judged the story's intent met. The aborted first attempt was caused by my input tooling, and it produced no assistant activity.

observations.description: Problem on my side: the adapter's `type` tool fails on any text starting with '-' ("command send-keys: invalid flag -"). On my first try the bullet lines were never typed, and my separate Enter presses sent a cut-off prompt (the intro paragraph only, no requirements). I interrupted with Escape before the assistant replied: the log had no assistant turn and nothing changed on disk. I then ran /clear and sent the full message in a new session (76896710-...). The aborted session 41e6eb5e-... is still on disk and should be ignored when grading.

The acceptance criterion names `superpowers:writing-plans`, but the plugin loaded from the worktree calls itself `hyperpowers` (skills show as /hyperpowers:...). A literal grep for `superpowers:writing-plans` will never match. The criterion or the grader should accept the hyperpowers namespace.

The workspace-trust and Bypass Permissions dialogs both have 'No, exit' selected by default, so a tester who just presses Enter exits. I had to press Down to pick the accept option each time. The first-run onboarding (theme picker, security notes) also appeared even though HOWTO says the config is pre-seeded with dialog-bypass state.
After each dialog the screen went fully blank for a moment before Claude Code drew its next view.

The user asked for an 'extreemly minimal POC' with no questions, yet the agent went through brainstorming → a written spec → a Codex review-gate preflight (Codex not installed) → writing-plans. That is a lot of process for a request explicitly asking for minimal, though it is what this story wants to see.
Before any auth code existed, the agent ran `npm install` on its own and created a .gitignore listing docs/hyperpowers, so the spec is not tracked by git.

criteria.criterion: The agent loaded superpowers:writing-plans (here named hyperpowers:writing-plans, since the plugin uses that namespace) before writing any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Session log home/.claude/projects/-Users-...-coding-agent-workdir/76896710-519d-4d60-b836-d44383d18d51.jsonl, tool calls in order: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"} → Bash (ls/cat app.js, npm install) → Write .gitignore → Write docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-auth-design.md → Reads/Bash of the code-review gate scripts → Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"} → text "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan." Before the Skill call, the only files written were .gitignore and the spec. `git status --short` afterwards showed only `?? .gitignore` and `?? package-lock.json`, and `find -newer package.json` found no new or changed .js files (app.js unchanged).
